title: Critical Outdoor System Fault
shortDescription: A critical fault in the outdoor unit has shut down the system.
fullDescription:
E200 on Lennox communicating heat pumps (iHarmony / iComfort) indicates a critical outdoor fault that required immediate shutdown. The specific sub-cause is logged in fault history and will typically appear alongside a sub-code (E202, E223, etc.).

Check the iComfort service menu for the secondary code.

fixSteps.title: Read fault history
fixSteps.instruction: Access Service > Alerts on the iComfort UI.

fixSteps.title: Follow sub-code
fixSteps.instruction: Troubleshoot using the secondary code's article.

whenToCallPro: Usually needed.

faq.a: Yes via breaker, but the sub-cause must be fixed.

title: Outdoor Unit Hardware Error
shortDescription: Outdoor control board detected internal hardware failure.
fullDescription: E202 indicates the outdoor board self-test failed. This is typically a failed control board that requires replacement.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut outdoor breaker 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Replace board if persistent
fixSteps.instruction: A tech will install a matching iHarmony control.

whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.a: No - matched to the outdoor model.

title: Outdoor Low Line Voltage
shortDescription: Outdoor unit detected line voltage below 187V.
fullDescription:
E223 is triggered when the outdoor control measures line voltage below safe minimum (~187V on 230V). Operation is blocked until voltage normalizes.

Causes include utility brownouts, loose connections at the disconnect, or a contactor issue.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 208-230V at outdoor disconnect.

fixSteps.title: Tighten lugs
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, tighten service lugs.

whenToCallPro: If voltage is fine but fault persists.

faq.a: Yes when voltage returns to normal.

title: Outdoor High Line Voltage
shortDescription: Outdoor unit detected line voltage above 253V.
fullDescription:
E224 is triggered when incoming line voltage exceeds ~253V. High voltage can damage the inverter and compressor, so the unit shuts down.

Call the utility or an electrician to investigate.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm high-voltage condition with a meter.

fixSteps.title: Contact utility
fixSteps.instruction: If service voltage is high, call utility.

whenToCallPro: Always if voltage truly high.

faq.q: Could it be a neutral problem?
faq.a: Yes - a broken service neutral can cause high phase voltage.

title: Outdoor Unit Communication Failure
shortDescription: iComfort/iHarmony bus lost communication with outdoor unit.
fullDescription: E290 means the indoor equipment interface cannot reach the outdoor unit over the RSBus. Typical causes are miswired terminals, missing outdoor power, or a failed outdoor communications chip.

fixSteps.title: Verify outdoor power
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm breakers on.

fixSteps.title: Check RSBus wires
fixSteps.instruction: Verify R, i+, i- and C continuity.

whenToCallPro: For board replacement.

faq.a: Lennox uses i+/i-/R/C labeling - match by name, not color.

title: Outdoor Unit Incompatible / Wrong Model
shortDescription: iComfort detected an incompatible outdoor unit.
fullDescription:
E294 means the outdoor unit doesn't match the indoor/equipment profile. This often appears after replacing one component with a non-matching model or after a firmware issue.

Re-run equipment setup and confirm compatibility on Lennox's AHRI matchup.

fixSteps.title: Re-run setup
fixSteps.instruction: On iComfort, Service > Installation Setup.

whenToCallPro: Usually needed.

faq.q: Can I mix older Lennox with iComfort?
faq.a: Only certain generations - consult Lennox matchup tool.

title: Compressor High Pressure
shortDescription: Compressor stopped due to high-pressure switch trip.
fullDescription:
E400 indicates the high-pressure switch has opened. Usually caused by dirty outdoor coil (cooling) or blocked indoor airflow (heating).

After multiple trips the system locks out with E410.

fixSteps.title: Clean outdoor coil
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse fins.

fixSteps.title: Clean indoor filter
fixSteps.instruction: Wash or replace.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning doesn't help.

faq.a: No - the switch protects the system.

title: Compressor Low Pressure
shortDescription: Low pressure switch open.
fullDescription: E403 indicates the low-pressure switch has tripped, usually from refrigerant loss. After 3 trips in an hour the system locks out with E412.

fixSteps.title: Call for service
fixSteps.instruction: Pro will perform leak search and charge correction.

whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.a: No - EPA license required and leak must be fixed.

title: High Pressure Lockout
shortDescription: Repeated E400 trips - system locked out.
fullDescription:
E410 is a lockout after the high-pressure switch opened three or more times. Manual reset required.

Fix the root cause (airflow or charge) before resetting.

fixSteps.title: Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Clean coil and filter.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle breaker.

whenToCallPro: If quick recurrence.

faq.a: Protects compressor from repeated stress.

title: Low Pressure Lockout
shortDescription: Repeated E403 trips - system locked out.
fullDescription: E412 occurs after multiple low-pressure trips. Manual reset required; root cause is almost always refrigerant loss.

fixSteps.title: Call pro
fixSteps.instruction: Leak search and recharge.

whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.q: Will it clear on its own?
faq.a: No, manual reset after repair.

title: Compressor Inverter Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor variable-speed compressor drive fault.
fullDescription:
E420 on Lennox variable-capacity heat pumps (like XP25) indicates an inverter drive fault - overcurrent, overtemperature, or drive communication error.

Usually requires drive or compressor diagnostics by a Lennox-trained technician.

fixSteps.title: Clean outdoor
fixSteps.instruction: Blow dust from heatsink fins.

fixSteps.title: Call technician
fixSteps.instruction: Requires drive diagnostic tool.

whenToCallPro: Always.

faq.a: Not always - often the inverter drive is the failure.

title: Outdoor Thermistor Open/Short
shortDescription: Outdoor air or coil thermistor is out of range.
fullDescription:
E433 means a Lennox outdoor temperature sensor has failed open or shorted. The sensors used are 10k ohm NTC thermistors.

Locate the indicated sensor (ambient or coil) and replace if resistance is out of range.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Shut disconnect.

fixSteps.title: Reseat or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 10k ohms at 25C.

whenToCallPro: If part isn't readily available.

faq.a: Ambient hangs free near intake; coil is clipped to a return bend.

title: Inverter Communication Loss
shortDescription: Communication lost between control and inverter board.
fullDescription: Error E105 on Lennox iComfort heat pumps means the main control cannot communicate with the inverter compressor drive. The system shuts down to protect the compressor.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect both indoor and outdoor power for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Check RSBus
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect 4-wire communication cable end to end.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat communication plugs at both boards.

fixSteps.title: Call Lennox Tech
fixSteps.instruction: Inverter board diagnostics require Lennox iComfort tools.

whenToCallPro: iComfort inverter systems require Lennox-trained technicians with proper diagnostic tools.

faq.a: Lennox's proprietary communication bus between equipment and thermostat.
Lennox specifies 18-gauge stranded thermostat cable for RSBus.
Inverter boards are $400-$700 plus labor.

title: Heating Outdoor Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor temperature sensor reading invalid.
fullDescription: E124 indicates the outdoor air temperature thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range, affecting defrost timing and balance point staging.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Locate Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Find OD sensor on cabinet or in airflow path.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wires
fixSteps.instruction: Check for chew damage or corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Measure Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Should match Lennox thermistor curve at ambient.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Two-wire screw mount sensor.

whenToCallPro: If wiring and resistance check fine, the control board input may have failed.

faq.a: Yes with default defrost timing and possible extra aux runtime.
Moderate - moisture intrusion at the connector is the typical culprit.
$30-$80 for OEM thermistor.

title: Liquid Line Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Refrigerant liquid-line temperature sensor failed.
fullDescription: E125 indicates the liquid-line thermistor used for charge management on iComfort heat pumps is invalid. Without it, advanced charge correction is disabled.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Find Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Located clamped to liquid refrigerant line at outdoor unit.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Clip
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure good contact with copper tubing.

fixSteps.title: Test Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to ambient line temp curve.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Lennox part with thermal grease.

whenToCallPro: If repair persists after sensor swap, the control board may need inspection.

faq.a: Yes, but you lose charge-assist accuracy.
Short term yes, but get it fixed at next service.
$40-$100 for sensor.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor coil thermistor reading out of range.
fullDescription: E180 reports that the coil-temperature sensor used for defrost initiation/termination is invalid, leading to incorrect defrost decisions.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Mount
fixSteps.instruction: Verify sensor sits firmly against coil hairpin.

fixSteps.title: Check Wires
fixSteps.instruction: Look for damage or rodent chew.

fixSteps.title: Measure Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Compare to coil temp curve.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor with thermal paste.

whenToCallPro: If coil ices repeatedly, the defrost board itself may need service after sensor replacement.

faq.a: It tells the control when to defrost and when to stop.
Only to its OEM location with proper thermal contact.
Most pros do it in under an hour.

title: High Pressure Switch Trip
shortDescription: High-side pressure switch opened.
fullDescription: E312 indicates the high-pressure switch tripped, shutting down the compressor to prevent damage from elevated discharge pressure.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
symptoms: Outdoor fan may not be spinning
Hot air not blowing through coil

fixSteps.title: Wash Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse outdoor coil with garden hose.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify outdoor fan spins freely and runs.

fixSteps.title: Clear Debris
fixSteps.instruction: Trim back vegetation 24" from unit.

fixSteps.title: Pro Service
fixSteps.instruction: Have charge and fan capacitor verified.

whenToCallPro: Repeated trips after coil cleaning indicate refrigerant or fan motor issues for a pro.

faq.a: Yes, sustained pressure damages the compressor.
Often yes if the coil was very dirty.
At least annually in spring.

title: Low Pressure Switch Trip
shortDescription: Low-side pressure switch opened.
fullDescription: E313 means the low-pressure switch tripped, suggesting low refrigerant or restricted indoor airflow leading to suction pressure below the safe threshold.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Filter Change
fixSteps.instruction: Replace filter; run fan-only to thaw ice.

fixSteps.title: Open Vents
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure all registers are open.

fixSteps.title: Visual Leak
fixSteps.instruction: Look for oil stains at fittings.

fixSteps.title: Call Tech
fixSteps.instruction: Leak search and repair require certification.

whenToCallPro: Low refrigerant always means a leak; have it located and repaired professionally.

faq.a: EPA cert required.
Restricted airflow lowers coil temp and pressure.
No - leaks worsen over time.

title: Reversing Valve Fault
shortDescription: Reversing valve did not change state.
fullDescription: E347 indicates the reversing valve failed to switch when commanded, leaving the heat pump in the wrong mode for the call.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
symptoms: Outdoor unit runs but indoor wrong

fixSteps.title: Verify Mode
fixSteps.instruction: Check thermostat mode setting.

fixSteps.title: Listen for Click
fixSteps.instruction: Solenoid should click on mode change.

fixSteps.title: Test 24V
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage at solenoid coil.

fixSteps.title: Call Pro
fixSteps.instruction: Replacement involves brazing and recovery.

whenToCallPro: Reversing valve replacement requires recovery, brazing, and recharge.

faq.q: Can a tech free a stuck valve?
faq.a: Sometimes by tapping with power applied; otherwise replace.
$700-$1500 commonly.
Usually covered if under 10 years.

title: Defrost Termination Fault
shortDescription: Defrost cycle did not terminate properly.
fullDescription: E370 indicates the defrost cycle exceeded its maximum time without coil temperature rising, suggesting sensor or refrigerant issues.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.
symptoms: Steam from outdoor unit for over 10 minutes

fixSteps.title: Check Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Verify coil sensor is firmly attached.

fixSteps.title: Listen to Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm reversing valve clicks at defrost start.

fixSteps.title: Pro Diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Tech should evaluate refrigerant and valve operation.

whenToCallPro: Persistent E370 usually requires technician evaluation of charge and defrost cycle timing.

faq.a: 2-10 minutes typically.
It signals when defrost is complete.
No - the coil will continue icing.

title: Outdoor Fan Lockout
shortDescription: Outdoor fan motor locked out after multiple failures.
fullDescription: E411 means the outdoor fan motor failed to start or maintain RPM multiple times, locking out the system to protect the compressor from high pressure.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Power Off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect outdoor power.

fixSteps.title: Spin Test
fixSteps.instruction: Manually spin fan blade - should rotate freely.

fixSteps.title: Capacitor Test
fixSteps.instruction: Discharge and read capacitance.

fixSteps.title: Replace Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new motor or capacitor as needed.

whenToCallPro: If capacitor is good and fan is stiff, motor replacement is needed - some are ECM and pricier.

faq.a: $150-$500 depending on type.
30-90 minutes for a pro.

title: Compressor Top Cap Trip
shortDescription: Compressor internal overload tripped.
fullDescription: E420 (compressor protection variant) indicates the compressor's internal thermal overload tripped, often due to high amperage or overheating from low refrigerant or high pressure.
safetyWarning: Always disconnect power at the breaker before opening any HVAC equipment. High-voltage circuits and refrigerant systems can cause serious injury.

fixSteps.title: Cool Down
fixSteps.instruction: Let unit sit 2 hours before retest.

fixSteps.title: Check Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace indoor filter to ensure airflow.

fixSteps.title: Wash Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Clean outdoor coil.

fixSteps.title: Pro Diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Refrigerant charge and amperage need professional measurement.

whenToCallPro: Repeated overload trips usually mean refrigerant or compressor problems for a pro.

faq.q: Will it restart on its own?
faq.a: Yes once internal thermal cools.
EPA cert required.
1-3 hours typically.
